chapter: Quincy Jones, films and harmonica heroes
title: Larry Adler as harmonica pioneer
summary: Toots praises Adler as the pioneer who made harmonica a show instrument, though not a jazz player.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, since you said English and you were talking about a harmonica player, let’s talk about Larry Adler.

No. No, no, Larry Adler. He was big-time then, you know. He was the biggest influence. He was… he was the pioneer on harmonica. And he was… if you look at YouTube, you’ll see a lot of him. I’m not making fun, you know, but he did it tastefully and well, and he convinced quite a few classical… [I mean?], he did even a duo with Itzhak Perlman, the handicapped violin virtuoso. I don’t know what his story… whether one of those big standards. And no, he did… But I met him a couple of times, but he was awesome as a performer. And he established the harmonica as a show… I mean, what he did… the harmonica became a show instrument, you know, implemented. [laughs] But he was fantastic at what he did. And he played. But then he got political, blacklisted or something. I have no knowledge or no opinion to say about that. But he was really the pioneer and a good… he played piano sometimes. Played the piano and the harmonica.
But he didn’t really play jazz.
Not jazz, no. You could listen to him on YouTube, you know. And no, but look, there’s… not everybody likes jazz or needs jazz, you know. [laughs] No.
